author: Russell Brand
description:
Nigel Farage called for the reintroduction of the death penalty after Henry Nowak's murder and the public agreed. But Russell Brand asks the question nobody wants to sit with — is this actually about justice or is it about anger, despair and sorrow being weaponized by the same corrupt leadership that created the conditions for this tragedy in the first place. The death of Henry Nowak is real. The grief is real. But Russell argues the people exploiting that grief have been failing Britain for decades and the death penalty is just the latest crisis being used to push the country toward something far more authoritarian.

author: Russell Brand
description:
By 2029 every worker in the United Kingdom will be required to have a digital ID or they will not be able to work. Russell Brand breaks down exactly what that means — because it is not about convenience and it is not about safety. The moment the government decides it does not like you, it can freeze your finances, block your travel and lock you out of the economy entirely. Russell calls it what it is. Perfect control. And they are going to sell it to you with a smile.

author: Russell Brand
description:
Russell Brand makes the argument that cuts through every political label — our true religion is not justice, not fairness, not liberalism. It is consuming. And the moment anyone threatens the endless flow of stuff, the people who claim to care most about the world go into a complete frenzy. We were made to love people and use things. Somewhere along the way that got flipped. And nobody wants to admit it because admitting it means looking at the void we have been filling with things instead of truth.

author: Russell Brand
description:
Russell Brand breaks down his favorite episode of The Chosen — the moment Simon Peter reaches the end of himself. Nothing left. No identity. No answers. Just complete brokenness. And it is precisely in that moment of total surrender that something extraordinary happens. Russell explains why this scene moved him so deeply and what it reveals about what it actually means to come to Christ — not when you are strong but when you have absolutely nothing left.
